senses.gloss: ch. same, to strike against; to knock, drive in. Targ. II Esth. VI, 10, sq.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 4:21">Targ. Jud. IV, 21</cite> (ed. Wil. <he>נקיש׳</he>); a. e.—
Snh. 25ᵇ אנא ידענא למִנְקַשׁ וכ׳ Ar. (ed. לנַקּוּשֵׁי, Pa.; Rashi בנְקָשָׁא) I know better how to clap (at the pigeon-race).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 52b:10">B. Kam. 52ᵇ</cite> <he>איבעי ליה למיזיל ומִינְקַשׁ עליה</he> it was his duty to go and knock upon it (to try the soundness of the board).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 59a:9">B. Mets. 59ᵃ</cite> (prov.) <he>כמִשְׁלַם … נָקֵישׁ ואזיל תיגרא</he> when the barley is gone out of the pitcher, quarrel knocks and comes in; a. e.

senses.gloss: <cite ref="N01251">same</cite>. Y. B. Bath. IV, end, 15ᶜ; Y. Gitt. III, end, 45ᵇ <he>מַקְּשִׁין על גרבא וכ׳</he> they knock at the vessel outside and know what is in it.
units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 6">Lev. R. s. 6</cite> <he>נסתיה … ואַקְּשֵׁיה לארעא</he> he took the cane and knocked it against the floor; a. e.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 30:19">Targ. Job XXX, 19</cite> (sec. Vers.).—

<cite ref="Zevachim 5b">Zeb. 5ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי חזית דאַקְּשַׁת … אַקְּשָׁהּ לחטאת</he> (ed. <cite ref="N01252"><he>אַקֵּישׁ</he></cite>) why do you compare it with peace offerings? Compare it with sin offerings; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 470">Yalk. Lev. 470</cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 15a:14">Snh. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>לאַקּוּשֵׁי וכ׳</he> to place on an equal footing &c.; a. e.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ecclesiastes 12:3">Targ. Koh. XII, 3</cite> (of the trembling hands of the age-stricken; h. text <he>התעותו</he>).

senses.gloss: to be set side by side, be compared.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 61a">Pes. 61ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 12:4">Ex. XII, 4</cite>) <he>א׳ אוכלין למנויין</he> those who partake of the Passover lamb are placed on an equal footing with those who are entered as shareholders, i.e. it must be slaughtered in behalf only of those entered and of such among them as are able to partake.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 15a">Snh. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>עבד א׳ לקרקעות</he> a slave is classed with landed estate.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 63a">Ib. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>אִיתַּקּוּשֵׁי אִיתַּקּוּשׁ</he> they (the bowing and the sacrificing to the idol) are legally alike; a. fr.
